page: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU configuration. It provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX (tile and int8). The system couples these 16 vCPUs with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a dense 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote network storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread responsiveness and capable matrix processing, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2000.0 (top 25%) and 373.33 tokens/sec in text generation on smaller 135M language models (top 10%). Broader compute and memory bandwidth workloads register within the middle 50% tier, showing 15985.02 in stress-ng multi-core and 83.49 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth. Passmark memory testing falls into the lower 25% bracket (1783.15), indicating that raw memory subsystem bandwidth may encounter contention compared to smaller footprint configurations.

By constraining the core count to 16 vCPUs while preserving the 256.0 GB memory footprint of an E32 class instance, the E32-16s_v6 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis. It is tailored for memory-bound relational databases, large in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing tasks that require substantial RAM allocations without necessitating the licensing expenses of higher core counts.
